sermon.title: Three Revelations Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Three Revelations Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues through the opening of Revelation, saying we need a hearing ear, that the book came from Jesus through an angel to all of His servants, and that angels do not give conflicting messages. He teaches that the blessing in Revelation 1:3 and 22:7 comes to those who read and keep the book, and then lays out what he calls sound doctrine, the foundational doctrines of Hebrews 6 and the mature doctrines of adding to faith.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The captions begin at 0:02. Editor notes on references: at about 4:49 he says a verse of the Quran is “in the book of [unclear] 16 and 26”; this is not a Bible reference and has not been checked by this site. At about 24:18 he says “in Revelations” for the words “Come out from among them”; those exact words are 2 Corinthians 6:17, and Revelation 18:4 says “Come out of her, my people,” so both passages are shown. He reads the passages in Hebrews 6, 2 Peter 1, Hebrews 9 and 1 Corinthians 12 without naming the chapter and verse, and reads past 1 Timothy 1:9 into verse 10; they are shown here for reference. He names other religious leaders, preachers, public figures and religions himself; the claims about them are his own opinions and have not been checked by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section.

chunks.section_question: Why is “he who has an ear, let him hear” repeated seven times, and how do we get a hearing ear?
chunks.short_answer: He says the repetition shows the message is that we need an ear to hear, and that besides wisdom and knowledge we should pray for a hearing ear. He says God is always talking to His church, but we haven’t been taught to come to hear Him; instead we have been taught to come for an inspirational message and an offering.

Why? ’Cause God’s talking to His church. He’s always talking to His church. But we don’t come to hear Him talk, because we haven’t been taught to come to hear Him

chunks.section_question: Why does he say true angels don’t change their messages?
chunks.short_answer: He says angels don’t have conflicting messages, Jesus doesn’t have a conflicting message, and the Holy Ghost doesn’t come with conflicting messages. He says that if John’s revelation were not backed up by the other scriptures, John would be seeing the wrong angel. He says another religion’s founder was told something that contradicts the Bible, and that “if the source is wrong, they are wrong.”
chunks.text:
See, angels don’t have conflicting messages. Jesus doesn’t have a conflicting message. It’s the same message all the time. Amen. Joseph Smith, an angel was supposed to talk to him. The angel told him that black people couldn’t get into the church, they were cursed. That’s a conflicting message, because, you know, the Bible tells us that out of every kind and tribe, tongue and nation, “I am bringing out that people for Myself.” Isn’t that right? And so the angel was wrong, and so Joseph Smith wasn’t seeing an angel of God, he was having a nightmare. Are you there?

This is important, very important. We’ve been dubbed into looking at Revelations wrong.

chunks.section_question: What are the foundational doctrines of Christ in Hebrews 6, and what kind of faith?

amen? And that’s a big doctrine: “I’m not under law, I’m under grace. I’m not under legalism.” In other words, I can sin and I’m okay? No. Sound doctrine is righteous doctrine. Can you say amen? chunks.section_question: What does he say about baptizing for the dead?

chunks.text: See, these doctrines affect the way you treat people and yourself. chunks.section_question: What does he conclude about the first verses of Revelation?
chunks.short_answer: He says Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not the beast or Satan, along with the judgment to come, which calls for the fear of God because everyone will give an account to Jesus Christ. He says the message is for all of God’s servants, that angels speak the same thing, and that those whose revelations conflict with God’s word are wrong; he ends by calling the church to commit to reading and keeping the Bible.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues.
Therefore “Come out from among them And be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch what is unclean, And I will receive you.”
Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written in it; for the time is near.

faqs.question: What is the message of “he who has an ear, let him hear”?
faqs.answer: He says that since it is repeated seven times, the message is that we need an ear to hear, and that we should pray for a hearing ear.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’

faqs.question: Do we need a guru or a “coach of life”?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible never says God placed “coaches of life” in the body, and that anyone being his coach other than Jesus would make him fall way short.

faqs.question: Is the book of Revelation for everyone?
faqs.answer: He says yes: Jesus sent His angel to testify these things to the churches, so the message is for all of us.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify to you these things in the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the Bright and Morning Star.”

faqs.question: What does Galatians 1:8 say about angels?
faqs.answer: He reads that if we or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel than the one preached, let him be accursed.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.

faqs.question: Do angels change their messages?
faqs.answer: He says no, angels don’t need to change their messages; they already have the right one. He says it is men who have to change.

faqs.question: Why did he wait to preach on Revelation?
faqs.answer: He says God had him not preach on it for years until he could get real truths in the book through his “cranial vacuum,” because he had been tainted by what he heard.

faqs.question: What does Revelation 1:3 promise?
faqs.answer: He reads that he who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy and keep what is written in it are blessed, for the time is near.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written in it; for the time is near.

faqs.question: Can a famous preacher’s prayer bring blessing without reading and obeying?
faqs.answer: He says no: God doesn’t break His principles for anybody, and people want the blessing without reading or obeying the book.

faqs.question: What forgives sins?
faqs.answer: He says it is the blood of Christ that forgives sins, and that you have to come to Him personally and get it.

faqs.question: Which laws does he say we are not under?
faqs.answer: He says the “we’re not under law” doctrine refers to the ceremonial laws, such as animal sacrifices, wearing only wool or linen, and planting mixed seeds, which pointed to truth and were fulfilled by Jesus. He says we are still under righteous laws.

faqs.question: Does “I’m not under law, I’m under grace” mean I can sin?
faqs.answer: He says no: sound doctrine is righteous doctrine.

faqs.question: What kind of faith does he say we should have?
faqs.answer: He says it is faith that God has the power to perform what He promised, not faith in our faith. He gives an example of someone whose faith in his faith had not fixed his finances.

faqs.question: Is anything higher than faith?
faqs.answer: He says the mature doctrines of adding to your faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance and brotherly kindness, are higher than faith because we are building on faith.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.

faqs.question: Who will we give an account to?
faqs.answer: He says we are going to give an account to Jesus Christ, not to a rabbi or the leader of another religion’s church.

faqs.question: Who does he say Revelation was written for?
faqs.answer: He says it was written for all of God’s servants, not the pastors, ministers, popes or priests, but for all of us.
